title: Targets made easier the year after a miss
question: When a target was missed, was next year's target lowered?
finding: Of 174 missed years that were followed by a published target, the next target was made easier 52 times (30%), kept the same 102 times and made harder 20 times. After a year in which the target was met it was eased 7% of the time. In 21 of the 52 cases the new target was set at or below the result already achieved in the missed year, so the following year started as a pass. 46 of the 52 cases fall outside the two pandemic years. 0 measures have no published target after the last missed year.
how: For each measure in the first screen, each missed year was paired with the target published for the following fiscal year, including targets already published for fiscal years 2026 to 2028. A target counts as eased when it moved in the easier direction: lower where higher is better, higher where lower is better.
limits: Lowering a target after a miss can be honest planning: a budget cut, the end of pandemic money or a change in how the measure is counted are all good reasons to expect less, and the dataset records none of these reasons. The comparison with years in which the target was met is the fair test of whether misses are treated differently. Measures retired from the dataset cannot be seen, so targets that were dropped altogether are undercounted.
